identity.evidence: All six 1254×1254 frames keep one faceless white anatomical athlete in white trainers, side-facing throughout. Violet chest and quadriceps remain the principal highlighted muscle groups.

anatomy.evidence: Arms and legs remain traceable through the six poses: knees flex for landing and tuck, elbows flex at push-up bottom, and the jump lifts both bent legs with arms overhead. No limb detaches or changes side.

equipment.evidence: Bodyweight burpee with no equipment. The white shoes retain their identity and the same floor reference across ground and jump frames.

contact.evidence: Frame 1 and 5 left shoe contact bottoms share y1065 and right shoes y1055; their bottom x spans differ by at most one native pixel. physics.evidence: The sequence lands in a crouch, plants palms and jumps feet back, lowers the chest, presses to plank, tucks feet forward, and jumps upward. The airborne pose returns to the crouch as a soft landing; the shoulders, hips and shoes stay aligned to one side view.

muscles.evidence: Chest and quadriceps use the strongest violet, with abdominal and front-shoulder support. Muscle fields remain attached to the same body regions in squat, plank, push-up and jump.

cueAgreement.evidence: The first cue now says to land softly and reach hands toward the floor, matching frame 1 where palms are not planted. Frame 2 says to plant palms before jumping feet back. Lower, press, tuck and jump captions match frames 3–6.
